title: NEET exam cancelled: CBI registers FIR, special team begins nationwide probe
author: ETV Bharat
text: NEET Exam Cancelled: CBI registers FIR, Special Team begins nationwide investigation The case has been filed on the basis of a written complaint received from the Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, Government of India. Published: May 12, 2026 at 1: 30 PM IST New Delhi: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has registered a case in connection with the alleged irregularities and paper leak in the conduct of NEET-UG 2026 examination. According to a CBI spokesperson, the case has been registered on the basis of a written complaint received from the Department of Higher Education, Ministry of Education, Government of India. The investigating agency said in an official statement that it has registered an FIR regarding the rigging and paper leak in this examination. It has been registered under sections of the Indian Penal Code for offences of criminal conspiracy, cheating, criminal breach of trust, theft and destruction of evidence. It also contains charges under the Prevention of Corruption of Parents Act and Public Examinations (Prevention of Improper Means) Act, 2024 and the National Informatics Agency (NTA) Notification of 10 May 2026.

text: There is going to be a re-examination (re-NEET) of NEET UG 2026 this morning, but deep resentment and uncertainty prevails in the minds of the students. title: NEET UG 2026 re-exam held amid tight security, know students'feedback
author: Ajay Tiwari
text: The re-examination of NEET UG 2026 conducted by National Testing Agency was successfully conducted on 21st June at thousands of centres across the country and abroad. The re-examination of NEET UG was conducted by National Testing Agency (NTA). The exam was held from 2.00 pm to 1.15 pm. This time stringent measures were taken to make the exam completely transparent, with more than 5000 students appearing at 14 centres across the country and lakhs of students appearing at 14 centres abroad. In view of the glitches last time, unprecedented security arrangements were made at the exam centres. Intensive frisking of students at the entrance and biometric verification was made mandatory. CCTV surveillance and jammer facility was deployed within the exam hall to prevent any kind of improper activity. Students were advised to reach the centre well before time so that there is no hindrance in the process. As per the initial reports and feedback from students, the question paper held on 3rd May this time was quite challenging as compared to the Physics part (Physics).

title: NTA's own experts leaked NEET-UG paper for money, claims CBI chargesheet
author: द वायर स्टाफ
text: New Delhi: In the alleged paper leak case of NEET-Under Graduate (UG) 2026, the CBI (Central Bureau of Investigation) has come to the conclusion that it was the result of a well-planned, multi-state criminal conspiracy, in which subject experts of the National Testing Agency (NTA) allegedly leaked confidential exam papers. These questions were passed on to candidates for large sums of money through a network of coaching operators, touts and middlemen. According to a New Indian Express report, the CBI has filed a chargesheet in the special CBI court at Rouse Avenue, naming 13 accused. These include three subject experts, coaching operators, middlemen and candidates employed by the NTA. All these accused have been charged under the Indian Penal Code (IPC), Prevention of Corruption Act and Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024. According to the chargesheet, the conspiracy was started by three subject experts of the NTA - Botany expert Manisha Mandhare (1A), Science expert Sanjay Vithal Kulkarni (2A), Chemistry expert Prahlad Kulkarni (3A).
